raw.assessment: The incumbent supports telephone/in-person reservations and staffed key collection; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Success is unestablished: total needs are unknown, three conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly (H4-O4, H4-O6). A plausible account is that useful access depends on matching timing/equipment and reliably communicating changes. The concrete limiting observation is six declined requests concentrated on Tuesday/Thursday evenings (H4-O3): 68% aggregate reservation occupancy (H4-O2) does not demonstrate spare capacity within acceptable windows. Late or missed bookings likewise do not establish recoverable rehearsal time.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one authoritative desk booking ledger, with uniquely identified reservations and read-back confirmation of changes, can reduce conflicting expectations while preserving phone and in-person access; the online copy would show when it was last synchronized.
openings.delta: Makes reservation state and change acknowledgment explicit within the existing volunteer/desk workflow.
openings.prediction: If divergent records or unacknowledged changes cause conflicts, discrepancies and duplicate room expectations should decrease; added confirmation work could instead worsen administrative load.
openings.probe: Trial within existing staffing: log each change once, confirm room/date/time verbally, and track copy discrepancies, conflicting arrivals, and total weekly administration. Judge the eight-week conflict and average-time targets directly.
assumptions: The desk and volunteer can share an authoritative ledger using existing resources.
Some conflicting expectations originate in recording or communication; the causes of two observed conflicts remain unknown.

openings.claim: Can existing rooms and hours satisfy at least 90% of stated rehearsal needs once acceptable windows, required duration, and equipment are recorded, with every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement protected?
openings.delta: Distinguishes a feasible allocation obscured by inherited bookings from a binding time/equipment bottleneck.
openings.prediction: A feasible schedule supports testing reallocation; a demonstrated unavoidable shortfall identifies a bottleneck that aggregate vacancy conceals. Failure to find a schedule alone would not prove infeasibility.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record needs and all acceptable alternatives, then construct a paper eight-week allocation with performances fixed, existing equipment/hours, and weekly entitlements protected. Count outside rehearsals only when their suitability and dependable access are confirmed.
assumptions: Contacts can report their groups' needs and acceptable alternatives accurately.
A 60-minute entitlement is a minimum, not evidence that it fulfills a group's entire need.

raw.assessment: Aggregate unused capacity does not establish that usable rehearsal windows exist. Equipment needs, acceptable alternatives and attendance causes remain unknown; neither proposed explanation is established by these synthetic observations.

openings.claim: Some nominally separate groups may depend on the same indispensable players. Overlapping reservations could therefore produce late starts or absences even when both rooms are available. Coordinating these dependencies might recover usable rehearsal time.
openings.delta: Treat necessary attendance across groups as a scheduling constraint alongside room availability.
openings.prediction: If this mechanism matters, affected sessions will coincide with another booking involving a shared indispensable player, and attendance will improve when those overlaps are removed within acceptable windows.
openings.probe: During the short contact conversations, ask whether each late or missed session involved such an overlap and whether the shared player was necessary. Compare these accounts with timely sessions. If supported, trial mutually accepted staggering and record punctual usable minutes, unmet needs and administration time.
assumptions: Shared membership exists and sometimes prevents rehearsal; both are unmeasured.
Any trial preserves requested weekly 60-minute access, acceptable windows, existing rooms, equipment and staffed hours, telephone/in-person changes, zero new fees and both performances.

openings.claim: A consented cycle of three or more booking exchanges might admit an excluded group where no direct two-group swap works: one group moves rooms, another changes time, and the resulting vacancy satisfies the excluded request. This is a candidate mechanism.
openings.delta: Search for linked exchanges across inherited bookings instead of considering each refusal as an isolated occupied slot.
openings.prediction: Recorded acceptable windows and equipment requirements will reveal at least one feasible exchange cycle that meets an additional need without reducing another group's satisfied needs; absence of such a cycle rejects this opening for these bookings.
openings.probe: Use contact conversations to mark acceptable alternatives and piano necessity. Compare direct swaps with short exchange cycles on paper. Implement only a fully consented cycle, confirm all assignments by phone or in person, reconcile both calendars before activation, and count additional needs met, conflicts and total administration minutes.
assumptions: Enough groups have compatible flexibility to form a useful cycle.
Exclude performance bookings; retain every requested weekly minimum and all room, equipment, opening-hour and fee constraints.
One-time coordination effort may prevent the eight-week administration average from meeting its target; measure it rather than assuming savings.

openings.claim: Authoritative ledger, reservation IDs, verbal change read-backs and dated online synchronization may prevent conflicting expectations.
openings.probe: Trial within staffing; measure conflicts and administration.
openings.uncertainty: Two conflicts have unknown causes; shared-ledger practicality and added workload remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Recorded needs may expose feasible reallocation or binding window/equipment scarcity.
openings.discriminator: A feasible allocation versus demonstrated unavoidable shortfall.
openings.probe: Ask contacts for duration, acceptable alternatives and equipment; construct eight-week paper allocation. Verify suitability and reliability before counting outside rehearsals.
openings.uncertainty: Reports may err; 60 minutes need not satisfy full need; unsuccessful search cannot prove infeasibility.

openings.claim: Shared indispensable players may cause overlapping groups' lateness or absence.
openings.discriminator: Attendance improves after supported overlaps are removed.
openings.probe: Compare missed/late and timely sessions through contact accounts; if supported, trial accepted staggering; measure usable minutes, unmet needs and administration.
openings.uncertainty: Shared membership and causal necessity are unmeasured.

openings.claim: Consented exchanges among three-plus bookings may satisfy excluded requests beyond direct swaps.
openings.discriminator: A cycle adds satisfied need without reducing another group's satisfaction; no cycle rejects this opening for these bookings.
openings.probe: Map acceptable windows/piano necessity; compare swaps and cycles. Obtain full consent, confirm assignments and reconcile calendars before activation; measure needs, conflicts and all coordination time.
openings.uncertainty: Compatible flexibility is unknown; setup may exceed administration target.

post_distill.decision: Probe hypotheses; synthetic observations establish none. Preserve two rooms/24 staffed hours, requested weekly minimum, phone/in-person access, equipment, no fees and both performances. Evaluate eight-week 90% needs, fewer than two conflicts and at most two administration hours weekly; aggregate vacancy or lateness proves no recoverable capacity.
